messages:
morgan: quick handoff thread for the 06:00-14:00 UTC shift — primary/secondary + known coverage gaps and the quick runbook pointers i promised. running a short bridge for 10m to pass context :wave:

oncall-bot: Pager #4282 (api-latency) triggered at 1945678800 - severity: P2 - affected: hosted-api-us-west - current status: investigating

morgan: primary = alex (til 10:00 UTC), secondary = riya. jules will be swing from 08:00-12:00 UTC. samir on standby for infra escalations. if anything spikes during the handoff call @alex immediately.

alex: got it. i'm primary for the morning. my plan: watch the latency dashboard (Console > Routes > /v1/generate) and run the quick KV/cache health checks every 15m.

riya: i'll own customer-impact comms and triage any user-facing errors. if rate limit errors look widespread i'll flip routing to dedicated fallback policy.

morgan: coverage gaps: we only have 1 dedicated pool in us-east until 09:30 due to maintenance window. autoscale to spare nodes is limited. so if traffic jumps, prefer model-variant fallback (gpt-neo-small -> gpt-neo-medium) before scaling.

jules: noted. i'll monitor the dedicated pool and watch for OOMs on node-3 (it's flaky during warmup).

morgan: quick runbook links (shortcuts):
- KV cache fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback
- API latency triage: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-latency-triage
- Dedicated pool OOMs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-pool-oom
- Paging & escalation: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging-escalation

morgan: TL;DR remediation steps to try first (in order):
1) Check Console > Token-level traces for the offending route (quick filter: route:/v1/generate, status:>=500).
2) Rehydrate KV cache for the affected model shard: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.local/kv/rehydrate -d '{"model":"mneo-v1","shard":2}'`
3) If persistent tail latency, enable prefix batching override for the route: toggle `batching.force_small` -> true (Console -> Routes -> Advanced).
4) If node OOMs present, drain node and trigger warm standby: `infractl node drain node-3 && infractl node warm-standby add node-7`
5) As last resort, change routing policy to model-variant fallback: `routing set /v1/generate fallback=gpt-neo-medium` then monitor error rate for 5m.

alex: i'll bookmark those commands. quick note on step 2: rehydrate can take ~30-90s per shard, so do it staged if many shards to avoid overload.

riya: customer comms template (short): "We're investigating elevated latency for text-generation in US regions. Our on-call team has applied fallbacks to reduce impact and will provide updates every 15 minutes." link: https://redwood.internal/status/templates/latency-brief

jules: if you get repeated 503s with `kq: kv miss + backend:slow` in logs, run this diagnostic and attach output to the incident:
```
jq -r '.entries[] | select(.status=="miss") | {shard,seq,latency_ms}' /var/log/kv-cache/metrics.json | head -50
```

samir: infra note — maintenance window ends 09:30 UTC, autoscale will be back to normal at ~09:45. until then, avoid rolling large canaries that add weight to the dedicated pool.

morgan: handoff checklist (very quick):
- [ ] alex accepted primary (confirmed)
- [ ] riya confirmed comms
- [ ] jules will monitor dedicated pool
- [ ] samir standby for infra escalations
- [ ] bridge open for 10m, then async updates on thread

alex: accepted. i'll post a 15min status update or sooner if anything shows up. starting first KV health check now.

oncall-bot: Reminder: Runbook "api-latency-triage" has known steps to clear long-tail locks — recommended by automation at 1945678930.

riya: thanks — i'll prep the customer update template and slot in metrics once alex reports.

morgan: perfect. if anyone needs to escalate to SRE, follow paging-escalation runbook (link above) — for infra P1 escalate to on-call lead and page PagerDuty group `#infra-p1`. otherwise use this thread for coordination. :white_check_mark:
